feature.title: L+2 learned heads vs native gate under the serving read policy (Stage 1)

brief.goal: An offline comparison, on the reused B0/B1 corpus, of native-gate L+2, T0 L+2 and T3 L+2. It uses the serving policy: a hard cap of one unique expert read per target layer per forward, plus a pre-registered sweep of mean-read budgets that allows the policy to abstain. Every number is computed on identical groups, residency snapshots, exclusions and denominators. The output names one frozen candidate policy per scorer for a later served comparison. It trains nothing and reads nothing from the locked test split.
criteria: A new driver writes only to a new output directory under `/mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/` and never writes inside the R1 run directory `/mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/b1-r1-20261012/`. It refuses an output path inside that directory.

Sanity check: rerunning cap 2 at mean budget 1.0 reproduces the saved `spike-l2/result.json` dev and calib points (reads, useful, eligible) exactly for gate, L2_T0 and L2_T3 on the same group set. If it does not, the run stops before producing cap-1 results.
For each scorer (gate, T0, T3) and each of dev and calib, the run produces:
the full cap-1 sweep curve (threshold, reads, useful, wasted, recall, precision);
the operating points at mean budgets 0 (read nothing), 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.00 reads per forward-layer, with the achieved read count reported next to each point;
per-point abstention rate (forward-layers with no read) and the counts of fully and partly covered layers.

The main comparison is restricted to the target layers the serving path can cover: biased target gate, layer+2 streamed. That is 38 of 40 rows. Groups outside that set are reported separately and appear in no headline number.

Learned-vs-gate differences are reported at matched achieved reads, with 95% paired whole-session bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples) on the recall difference and the useful-read difference. Precision is reported but never used alone.
DSpark breakdown for every operating point:
anchor-only, draft-only and shared eligible rows and the recall on each;
coverage by live block width. Shared experts count once. The report states that no ordinary-decode dataset exists, so nothing here measures ordinary decode.

Each scorer's complete inference cost at cap 1 is measured on its actual L+2 checkpoint (T0, T3), six live tokens, under a CUDA graph, with its scope stated. The cap-1 timing replay charges each scorer its own measured delay, not the L+1 candidate's.

A `REPORT.md` and `result.json` hold all of the above, with exact commands, checkpoint hashes and artifact paths. Every number carries one of the labels "observed offline", "replay estimate" or "hypothesis".

C2 sanity reuses r1_l2_spike exactly. Score the cap-1 scorers' cached block scores; do not re-score.

The D2 native cap-1 scorer is a new GroupScorer in the new module. It is the best margin over tokens of each token's best available expert: b1_score._margin_values with k=1 on the gate's token scores and the r1_groups.skip_mask. items.body:
### Driver
`l2_cap1_eval.py RUN_DIR --dataset D --corpus C --b1-head H --out OUT [--device cuda]`. It loads the plan,
exclusions, `stages/l2/result.json` and the stamp windows as `r1_l2_spike.run` does, reusing its loaders. It filters
groups to serving-covered targets, builds the three scorers (plus T0 best_cap1), scores every dev and calib group
once, and caches the block scores in OUT. Then it:
- runs the cap-2 sanity check;
- produces the cap-1 sweeps, budget points, reports, bootstrap and replay;
- writes `OUT/result.json` and `OUT/REPORT.md`.

### Policy and curves
`r1_policy.sweep`/`best_under_budget`/`calibrate_threshold` are reused with `cap=1`. The new module adds:
- the budget-list loop;
- the explicit read-nothing point;
- curve export;
- matched-read lookup: for a target read count, the curve point with the nearest achieved reads, with both counts
  reported.

### Metrics
`r1_metrics.policy_report` is reused for the pooled, layer, stratum, session, positions and rowset cells. It gains an
optional `width:<n>` key and the abstention and covered-layer counts. A matched-candidate diagnostic splits each
learned head's useful reads into rows inside and outside the gate's top 12.

### Uncertainty
`session_bootstrap` is extended, keeping its default behaviour, to also return a CI on the useful-read difference. It
is run per budget point and per matched-read pair.

### Cost
`r1_cost` gains a `--cap` argument (default 2, so R1 records are unchanged). It is run at cap 1 on `T0_seed0.pt` and
`T3_seed0.pt` for one representative streamed target layer, six tokens, CUDA graph, reporting complete, head-only and
gate-only medians. The replay's delays are taken from these results.

items.body:
# L+2 learned heads vs native gate under the serving read policy (Stage 1)

## Goal
An offline comparison, on the reused B0/B1 corpus, of native-gate L+2, T0 L+2 and T3 L+2. It uses the serving
policy: a hard cap of one unique expert read per target layer per forward, plus a pre-registered sweep of mean-read
budgets that allows the policy to abstain. Every number is computed on identical groups, residency snapshots,
exclusions and denominators. The output names one frozen candidate policy per scorer for a later served comparison.
It trains nothing and reads nothing from the locked test split.

## Acceptance criteria
- A new driver writes only to a new output directory under `/mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/` and never writes inside the R1
  run directory `/mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/b1-r1-20261012/`. It refuses an output path inside that directory.
- Sanity check: rerunning cap 2 at mean budget 1.0 reproduces the saved `spike-l2/result.json` dev and calib points
  (reads, useful, eligible) exactly for gate, L2_T0 and L2_T3 on the same group set. If it does not, the run stops
  before producing cap-1 results.
- For each scorer (gate, T0, T3) and each of dev and calib, the run produces:
  - the full cap-1 sweep curve (threshold, reads, useful, wasted, recall, precision);
  - the operating points at mean budgets 0 (read nothing), 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.00 reads per forward-layer, with
    the achieved read count reported next to each point;
  - per-point abstention rate (forward-layers with no read) and the counts of fully and partly covered layers.
- The main comparison is restricted to the target layers the serving path can cover: biased target gate, layer+2
  streamed. That is 38 of 40 rows. Groups outside that set are reported separately and appear in no headline number.
- Learned-vs-gate differences are reported at matched achieved reads, with 95% paired whole-session bootstrap CIs
  (10,000 resamples) on the recall difference and the useful-read difference. Precision is reported but never used
  alone.
- DSpark breakdown for every operating point:
  - anchor-only, draft-only and shared eligible rows and the recall on each;
  - coverage by draft position (0 = anchor);
  - coverage by live block width.
  Shared experts count once. The report states that no ordinary-decode dataset exists, so nothing here measures
  ordinary decode.
- Each scorer's complete inference cost at cap 1 is measured on its actual L+2 checkpoint (T0, T3), six live tokens,
  under a CUDA graph, with its scope stated. The cap-1 timing replay charges each scorer its own measured delay, not
  the L+1 candidate's.
- A `REPORT.md` and `result.json` hold all of the above, with exact commands, checkpoint hashes and artifact paths.
  Every number carries one of the labels "observed offline", "replay estimate" or "hypothesis".

## Decisions
- Scorers are native gate at horizon 2 (no floors), `T0_seed0.pt` (sha e6f7661d…) and `T3_seed0.pt` (sha
  e675e2bd…) from `stages/l2/result.json`. `T0_seed0_best_cap1.pt` is evaluated as a secondary T0 row because it is
  the checkpoint chosen for cap-1 recall. T1, T2, T5 and G0 are not evaluated.
- The native arm's cap-1 block policy is the best margin over tokens of each token's best available expert. This
  matches serving per-token 1 and per-layer 1. The learned heads rank all available experts, not only the gate's top
  12. A matched-candidate diagnostic splits each learned head's gain into gain from rows the gate's top 12 holds and
  gain from rows outside it.
- Mapping a block head into serving: per source record, publish at most one entry (the head's top available expert)
  with its block score in the margin field. The calibrated global threshold is expressed as an identical per-row
  `min_margin`. This is recorded as the interface Stage 3 must implement, not built here.
- Budget points use the existing rule: best recall within the budget on dev, then the lowest feasible threshold within
  the budget on calib, recalibrated on calib's own sweep. That rule carries over unchanged; only the cap and the
  budget list change.
- The timing replay keeps R1's model (2.2 ms row read; contention zero/nominal/adverse = 1/2/3) at cap 1. It also
  runs once with zero scorer delay as a sensitivity check.
- New code lives beside R1 in `analysis/dsv41-drive/prefetch-replay/` as new modules. Existing modules change only to
  add parameters whose defaults keep R1/R2 behaviour byte-identical (cap passed in instead of hard-coded, an extra
  `width:<n>` cell key, bootstrap fields).

## Rules
- Never write into `b1-r1-20261012/`, `b1-r2-20261012/` or the F108 directories, and never rewrite their verdicts.
- Never open the locked test split. `read_r1_groups` already refuses it, and that refusal stays.
- No training. Checkpoint and plan sha256s are verified on load and recorded.
- divix01 run protocol:
  - pushed commit, private `wt-*` worktree, `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python`, print `sglang.__file__`;
  - CPU work under `taskset -c 0-63` with `OMP_NUM_THREADS`; GPU work under `flock cc-gpu.lock taskset -c 32-63`;
  - outputs on `/mnt/nvme1`;
  - run only the affected test files and record each exit status.
- Production on divix01 is untouched, and nothing runs in `dsv41-direct-prod`.

## Non-goals
- Optimising the learned scorer's inference path (Stage 2), serving integration or a served A/B (Stage 3).
- The F108 reverse order, native L+2 margin floors, L+4, new training, T5/G0 reruns.
- Changing production defaults.

- The serving candidate per scorer is chosen on dev, then frozen before calib is used to set its threshold. Pick the
  smallest budget in {0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00} whose nominal-contention replay on-time useful rows are within 5% of
  budget 1.00's. If no smaller budget qualifies, use budget 1.00. The choice, and the dev numbers that justify it, are
  written to `result.json` as `frozen_candidate`. The owner chose this rule.

## Open questions

## Design

### Driver
`l2_cap1_eval.py RUN_DIR --dataset D --corpus C --b1-head H --out OUT [--device cuda]`. It loads the plan,
exclusions, `stages/l2/result.json` and the stamp windows as `r1_l2_spike.run` does, reusing its loaders. It filters
groups to serving-covered targets, builds the three scorers (plus T0 best_cap1), scores every dev and calib group
once, and caches the block scores in OUT. Then it:
- runs the cap-2 sanity check;
- produces the cap-1 sweeps, budget points, reports, bootstrap and replay;
- writes `OUT/result.json` and `OUT/REPORT.md`.

### Policy and curves
`r1_policy.sweep`/`best_under_budget`/`calibrate_threshold` are reused with `cap=1`. The new module adds:
- the budget-list loop;
- the explicit read-nothing point;
- curve export;
- matched-read lookup: for a target read count, the curve point with the nearest achieved reads, with both counts
  reported.

### Metrics
`r1_metrics.policy_report` is reused for the pooled, layer, stratum, session, positions and rowset cells. It gains an
optional `width:<n>` key and the abstention and covered-layer counts. A matched-candidate diagnostic splits each
learned head's useful reads into rows inside and outside the gate's top 12.

### Uncertainty
`session_bootstrap` is extended, keeping its default behaviour, to also return a CI on the useful-read difference. It
is run per budget point and per matched-read pair.

### Cost
`r1_cost` gains a `--cap` argument (default 2, so R1 records are unchanged). It is run at cap 1 on `T0_seed0.pt` and
`T3_seed0.pt` for one representative streamed target layer, six tokens, CUDA graph, reporting complete, head-only and
gate-only medians. The replay's delays are taken from these results.

## Testing
- CPU unit tests on synthetic groups:
  - the budget loop, including the read-nothing point and the hard cap of 1;
  - the coverage filter, which drops unbiased targets and reports them separately;
  - the `width:<n>` cell;
  - the matched-read lookup;
  - the bootstrap's useful-read CI;
  - the refusal of an output path inside the R1 run directory;
  - unchanged defaults: R1's existing `test_r1_policy`, `test_r1_metrics`, `test_r1_stage1` and `test_r1_timing`
    stay green.
- GPU test: `r1_cost` at cap 1 selects at most one row per group and matches the reference read set.
- End to end on divix01: the cap-2 sanity reproduction against the saved spike points is the integration check.
